ARB Info

Arbitrum is a layer 2 scaling solution designed for the Ethereum network. Its goal is to increase the scalability of Ethereum while preserving its decentralization and security.

Arbitrum operates by batching many transactions together off-chain and then submitting a single, combined proof of all these transactions to the Ethereum base layer. This greatly reduces the amount of computation and storage that the Ethereum network has to handle, allowing it to support a much higher throughput of transactions.

data.title: CRWV, IREN, NBIS Stocks Extend Neocloud Selloff As Anthropic IPO Rally Fades - Michael Burry Takes A Victory Lap
data.description:
Key points:
  • NBIS led the drop, falling 4.4% in overnight trading, while IREN and CRWV fell 3% and 4%, respectively.
  • Michael Burry indicated that weakness is unrelated to the Nvidia fallout and the Democratic win in the midterms.
  • Retail sentiment for CRWV dipped to ‘extremely bearish’ from ‘bearish,’ and the sentiment for NBIS dipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral.’ 

CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS), and Iren Ltd. (IREN) extended their selloff on Thursday without a clear trigger, signaling continued concerns over the durability of the neocloud sector.

Anthropic (ANT) dipped 5% in overnight trading after its blockbuster IPO and debut rally appeared to add pressure. NBIS led the drop, falling 4.4%, while IREN and CRWV fell 3% and 4%, respectively.

Fueled by surging demand for cloud services, neocloud stocks rallied for much of the year. But over the past two months, sentiment has weakened amid doubts about the durability of Big Tech’s cloud spending, neocloud companies’ debt-fueled business models and a broader retreat from AI stocks.

So far this week, the neocloud trio shed 12% to 24%.

Burry Sees Fundamental Weakness

As neocloud and AI-linked stocks fell, investor Michael Burry called a victory lap. “Coreweave, Nebius, NVIDIA, semis, I tried to warn you all. I didn’t say short. But I provided the information one would need to sell,” he said in an X post.

Burry even got into a riff over his positions. When Futurum Equities’ chief market strategist Shay Boloor hinted that “The Big Short” investor did not warn about a neocloud rout from a Democrats win in Texas, and the fallout from former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affairs, Burry hit back: “If you think this is still all about an affair and some politics, you're not thinking hard enough.”

His comments appear to suggest weakness in AI-linked stocks stems from fundamentals and other factors, rather than those highlighted by Boloor.

Meanwhile, hedge fund manager Eric Jackson said the bearish case on neocloud companies has merit, but reading Anthropic’s S-1, he said investors may be overlooking signs of demand.

“The bears make compelling arguments about tightening credit, GPU depreciation, circular financing and the sheer amount of capital being deployed. But here's what they might be missing: 900% net revenue retention. Nearly 8x growth in $100K+ customers in nine months. Claude Cowork adoption outpacing Claude Code at the equivalent stage,” he said in an X post.

“I don't think every neocloud survives. But the best-capitalized ones could become substantially bigger businesses than Wall Street currently imagines.”

CRWV, IREN, NBIS Earnings Recap

CoreWeave’s Q3 revenue jumped 168% to $3.66 billion, beating estimates, and the company raised its 2026 revenue forecast. Its backlog reached $132.5 billion, and borrowing and spending also swelled.

Nebius’ revenue rose 571% to $980.8 million, above estimates, but third-party capacity delays forced the company to lower its 2026 sales outlook.

Iren’s revenue was $228 million, up 66% sequentially. The company faced a delay in bringing certain capacity online, which led its customer, Microsoft, to spend less than it had earmarked last quarter.

CRWV, NBIS Retail Sentiment Dips

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for CRWV dipped to ‘extremely bearish’ from ‘bearish’ and the sentiment for NBIS dipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral.’ The sentiment for IREN remained ‘neutral.’

“$NBIS People buy now and hold for long, these stocks are the ones people win in their life. I am going all in,” said a trader.

On the CRWV stream, a trader wrote, “Bullish setup for tomorrow. This has to be bottom.”

One of CoreWeave’s co-founders investing $30 million in the company’s bond was also being discussed.

data.title: Kenya says two hippos died after eating maize, fishing nets
data.description:
Two Kenyan hippopotamuses died after ingesting fishing nets and maize stalks, the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) said, joining a spate of deaths of wildlife after adverse contacts with humans.

A post-mortem examination had revealed one hippo, a young adult female, had "a compacted mass of discarded synthetic fishing nets that had caused a complete physical blockage at the junction between the stomach and small intestine," KWS said in a statement on X on Thursday.

KWS said an examination of the other hippo, an adult female, showed gas buildup in the animal's stomach had severely compressed its lungs.

"Maize stalks were observed among the stomach contents and may have contributed to dietary overload and excessive fermentation," KWS said.

KWS appealed to fishermen and local communities to avoid irresponsible handling and disposing of fishing nets and exposure of wildlife to dangerous food materials. It did not say when the animals, from Lake Naivasha in central Kenya, had died.

In August, Kenya said at least 18 elephants had likely died from cyanide poisoning due to the ingestion of pesticide-contaminated tomatoes from farms bordering Kenya's Amboseli ecosystem.

Fiona, a Nile hippo who became a viral online sensation after the Cincinnati Zoo chronicled her survival following premature birth nearly a decade ago, died on Thursday after eating a winter hat that fell into her habitat last week.

data.title: Reduce Tata Technologies; target of Rs 670: Prabhudas Lilladher
data.description:
Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Tata Technologies

TATATECH outlined an ambitious growth roadmap at its investor day. The company targets to reach USD1.1–1.3bn revenue by FY30, implying 15–20% CAGR over FY26–30, alongside operating EBITDA margin expansion to 20%+. The strategy centers on moving up the engineering value chain through larger full-vehicle programs (FVP), deeper engagement across product, plant and performance, and scaling its Aerospace and IHM businesses, supplemented by selective capability-led acquisitions and AI-led productivity. The management expects Automotive Services, Aerospace and IHM to deliver 15–18%, 25–30% and 15–18% CAGR, respectively, over FY26–30, with Aerospace and IHM contributing to over 20% of services revenue by FY30. The Software business is also expected to double from USD100mn in FY27E to USD200mn by FY30, while share of outcome-based engagements is targeted to exceed 50% of revenue. AI is expected to support both differentiation and operating leverage, with over 1,600 AI agents deployed and the management estimating a 50bps positive impact on operating margin at the FY27 exit run-rate. On the profitability front, the company expects operating EBITDA margin to improve from 15.7% in FY26 to ~17% by Q4FY27 and 20%+ by FY30, driven by favorable volume and mix, delivery efficiencies, AI-led productivity and G&A leverage, partly offset by investments in talent, business development and infrastructure. We believe the strategy offers multiple growth engines and scope for deeper customer relationships. However, achievement of the FY30 targets hinges on converting the pipeline into sustained growth over the longer term, which we feel will be challenging given the company’s historically volatile revenue trajectory amid the cyclical and highly competitive nature of the automotive industry.

Outlook

Hence, we maintain our estimates, TP and ‘REDUCE’ rating, as we believe the positives are already priced in.

data.title: Could Tesla Become The Next Lumentum? Gary Black Warns A SpaceX Stock Deal Could Send TSLA Down 25%
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gary Black warned that even with a 24% premium, an all-stock SpaceX bid could leave TSLA 25% below its current price within a month.
  • Black estimated the deal could dilute SPCX holders by about 50%, with selling pressure on the stock potentially further eroding the bid’s value. 
  • Hurlston defended the deal, citing growing demand for fiber-optic connections in AI data centers.

Shares of Lumentum (LITE) have fallen more than 40% since word of Marvell’s bid surfaced, and as CEO Michael Hurlston defended the deal on Thursday, analyst Gary Black warned that Tesla investors could face a similar reversal if SpaceX pays in stock.

MRVL Slide Wipes Out LITE Stock’s Premium

When Marvell Technology (MRVL) agreed to buy Lumentum Holdings (LITE) earlier this month, it offered 4.5 of its shares for every Lumentum share. At Oct. 28 closing prices, before news of the talks surfaced, the offer was worth about $1,132 per Lumentum share, a 24% premium to Lumentum’s closing price of about $914.

The deal fixed the number of Marvell shares Lumentum investors would receive, so the offer's value fell along with Marvell’s stock. By Thursday’s close, Marvell was trading at $138.47, putting the offer’s value at about $623 per Lumentum share. Black put Lumentum’s share price even lower, at around $535, which is 41% below its Oct.28 close. The companies expect the deal to close in the first half of 2028.

Why Black Thinks A Tesla Deal Rally Could Fade

Black first drew the Tesla comparison on Nov. 2, when Lumentum was trading around $750. By Nov. 4, he noted, Lumentum had fallen 27%, and Marvell had lost 31% from their Oct. 28 closing prices.

Now, his latest warning goes a step further. If SpaceX (SPCX) offered its own shares for Tesla (TSLA), Black said, Tesla could rally on the news and still end up 25% lower within a month. Black used $374 per Tesla share as his starting point. A 24% premium would put a hypothetical SpaceX bid at about $464 per share on paper. But issuing enough stock to buy Tesla could dilute existing SpaceX shareholders by about 50%, he estimated.

Black also said traders could sell SpaceX shares to lock in profits after the deal is announced. If that selling pushed SpaceX stock lower, the shares offered to Tesla investors would be worth less.

“The same dynamic is likely when $SPCX offers a +24% premium for $TSLA using SPCX stock as currency: TSLA investors will get a short-term pop on the deal headline and then experience quick downward pressure on $TSLA stock as investors sell $SPCX to try to lock in profits,” Black said on X.

If this pattern played out, Black estimated Tesla could trade at $280 within a month, 25% below his $374 starting price. Both companies have formed independent board committees to explore a merger.

LITE CEO Looks To Earnings To Win Back Shareholders

“We’ve got work to do with our shareholders,” Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston told Jim Cramer on CNBC’s Mad Money. Hurlston said that the shift from copper wiring to fiber-optic connections inside AI data centers is what makes the deal attractive. Marvell supplies the networking chips, while Lumentum makes the optical components that carry data between them.

Hurlston said demand remained strong after Lumentum’s quarterly revenue more than doubled from a year earlier. “Their numbers are phenomenal. Our numbers are phenomenal, and we feel the combination is even more powerful,” he said.

Hurlston pointed to Marvell’s Dec. 1 earnings report, Lumentum’s next results and an upcoming merger filing as opportunities to win back investors. “I think we’re going to get that multiple back once we can show our numbers and show how strong the two businesses are doing,” he said.

Retail Traders Weigh Cost Of Staying In MRVL-LITE Deal

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘neutral’ on both SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA), with ‘normal’ message volume for SpaceX and ‘low’ volume for Tesla. Meanwhile, sentiment was ‘bearish’ on both Marvell (MRVL) and Lumentum (LITE) amid ‘low’ message volume for both stocks.

One user said Lumentum should cancel the deal. Another user said they would rather see the company pay the breakup fee and seek a buyer willing to offer around $1,200 a share.

View this Stocktwits post

A separate user still counted Lumentum among five stocks they believed could beat the market over five years, while flagging the Marvell merger as the risk in owning it.

View this Stocktwits post

So far this year, TSLA is down nearly 17%, while SPCX trades 2.5% above its June IPO price. Despite their declines since news of the deal surfaced, MRVL is still up about 63% and LITE is up 45%.

data.title: Copper slides; London prices head for sixth straight weekly decline
data.description:
Copper prices fell sharply on Friday, with London copper on track for a sixth consecutive weekly decline, pressured by concerns over AI-related demand, bets for higher interest rates and reduced expectations of US copper tariffs.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 3% to $12,142 a metric ton by 0555 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since March. Prices have fallen over 9% this week.

The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SCFv1) was down 3.6% at 92,120 yuan ($13,806.54) a ton after touching its lowest level since December 2025. The contract has slipped over 12% so far this week.

A Democratic victory in the US midterms sparked concerns over the pace of AI infrastructure spending and lowered expectations for US copper import tariffs. The red metal is used extensively in AI-related infrastructure, including data centres and power grids.

"The tariff trading is dying. We are seeing a huge amount of material leaving the US for China. That has started to diminish the expectation of things," said Albert Mackenzie, a copper analyst at Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.

People with knowledge of the matter said that surging premiums for refined copper in China against exchange benchmark prices have prompted some traders to ship metal from the US to the world's largest consumer.

The Yangshan premium (SMM-CUYP-CN), a gauge of China's appetite for imported copper, was at record-high levels.

"There's more and more evidence that the AI investment boom is waning and that the US Fed is going to have to get more aggressive with policy to control inflation. It's impacting the demand outlook for copper, with the commodity also weighed down by a firming US dollar," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

The dollar hovered near a 19-month peak. A stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated metals more expensive for holders of other currencies, while higher rates tend to weigh on growth-linked metals.

Asian shares were on track for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investors' faith in AI trades.

Among other LME metals, aluminium fell 0.9%, zinc fell 2.1%, lead lost 0.6%, nickel slipped 0.4% and tin dropped 2.3%.

On the SHFE, aluminium (SAFv1) fell 0.8%, zinc (SZNv1) declined 1%, lead (SPBv1) lost 0.6%, nickel (SNIv1) slipped 2.3% and tin (SSNv1) slid 4.3%.

data.title: Evonik CEO Says BASF Ending Takeover Pursuit Removes Source of Uncertainty
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Evonik Industries' interim Chief Executive Officer Claus Rettig said BASF's decision to abandon efforts to take over the German chemicals company removes a source of uncertainty for its employees.

"Our plan for the coming years is set. Now we can focus our full energy on Evonik's standalone development," Rettig said. "For our employees, this removes a source of uncertainty."

BASF said Thursday that it would end its pursuit of Evonik after two all-cash offers were rebuffed.

"We are convinced that BASF's derisked all-cash offer of 24 euros per share would have represented significant additional value for Evonik shareholders," BASF Chief Executive  Markus Kamieth said.

The bid valued Evonik at 11.18 billion euros ($12.26 billion), based on share-count data provided by FactSet.

data.title: Australian shares slide to six-month low, dragged by miners, banks and tech
data.description:
Key points:
  • ASX200 hits six-month closing low
  • Worst weekly fall since June 2022
  • Miners lost nearly 13% on week

By Anjali Singh

Australian shares slid to a near six-month low on Friday, dragged lower by miners, financials and tech stocks as weak global risk sentiment set the tone and rising local unemployment pointed to slower wage growth and a sharper economic slowdown.

The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index fell 1.6% to 8,592.6, dropping over 5% on the week, its steepest weekly decline since June 2022.

Weak jobs data led investors to pare bets on further rate hikes, but sentiment soured as the market weighed whether the Reserve Bank of Australia's five rate hikes this year had squeezed the economy too hard. A string of recent job cuts has added to that concern.

"The rising trend in unemployment and increasing reports of layoffs are consistent with rate hikes, high fuel prices and poor confidence working to slow the economy," AMP's Chief Economist Shane Oliver said in a report.

Financials retreated 1.6% to a near one-month low, with the Big Four banks each shedding between 1% and 2.2%. The sector fell more than 3% this week, marking its worst week since mid-August.

Miners weakened 2.2% to their lowest since March as copper prices hit a near eight-month low and bullion headed for its worst week in eight months. Heavyweight BHP gave up 1.8%. The sub-index logged its worst week since March 2020, falling nearly 13%.

Gold stocks tumbled 4.5%, with Northern Star Resources and Evolution Mining losing 3.7% and 4.8%, respectively.

Technology stocks tanked 4.7%, tracking losses in US peers after Anthropic's debut failed to revive investor faith in the sector.

"Australian tech gets punished on bad days because it's high-multiple and doesn't trade much, not because local fundamentals have changed," said Philip Deloughery, head of equities at MPC Markets.

Across the Tasman Sea, the New Zealand benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 1% to 14,107.41 points.

data.title: China Retains Key Loan Prime Rates
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - China retained its loan prime rates for the eighteenth consecutive month, as widely expected, on Friday.

The People's Bank of China left its one-year loan prime rate unchanged at 3.0 percent. Likewise, the five-year LPR, the benchmark for mortgage rates, was maintained at 3.50 percent.

The bank had reduced its both LPRs by quarter points in October 2024 and 10 basis points each in May 2025.

The decision came after economic data showed signs of slowdown towards the end of the year.

Official data showed that industrial output and retail sales growth eased more than expected to 4.8 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively in October. Moreover, the decline in fixed asset deepened to 8.1 percent in the January to October period.

data.title: India eyes 162.5% Scotch duty, testing U.K.-India trade pact - Reuters
data.description:
Just months after coming into force, the India-U.K. trade agreement is reportedly facing its first major challenge, with New Delhi opposing the extension of preferential tariff rates to bulk Scotch whisky imports.

Duty on bulk Scotch whisky imports was expected to be slashed to 75% and then gradually to 40% over 10 years as per the trade agreement. However, a Reuters report Thursday said that India now plans to levy a 162.5% duty on these imports, higher than the 150% in place before the trade deal.

Amid the confusion over tax rates, thousands of liters of bulk Scotch in more than 80 shipping containers belonging to Pernod, Diageo, and Bacardi are stuck at Indian ports, according to Reuters.

But in the first major dispute linked to the India-UK pact, Indian investigators have argued companies are using wrong customs classifications in importing bulk Scotch concentrates - these are deemed to be raw material used to make drinks like blended whiskies.

Since May, such imports, Indian ​investigators argue, come under a newly created customs line for so-called “compound alcoholic preparations", which attracts a 150% tariff, the report said. These imports then attract a consumption tax, which takes the full duty amount to 162.5%, ​according to a government document reviewed by Reuters and sources.

Under a so-called provisional release pending investigation, duty at ​75% of the goods’ value needs to be paid up front, with the rest covered by bank guarantees, the sources said.

"Industry has already reduced prices of Scotch products in the market when the India-UK pact kicked ​in, and now they are faced with higher duties again," said a source in the liquor importing business.

Pernod, which owns UK-based Chivas Brothers, Diageo, and many other Indian companies, believes Scotch imports - bulk and bottled both - should be taxed only at 75% as per the trade pact.

The British government has repeatedly said in statements it is working with New Delhi on the issue, while India has said the dispute will be resolved soon, the report added.

Elsewhere, the top-selling American whiskey brands include Brown-Forman's (BF.A) (BF.B) Jack Daniel's, Woodford Reserve, Old Forester, and Jack Daniel's Tennessee Honey, as well as Suntory's Jim Beam and Maker's Mark, Heaven Hill Brands' Evan Williams, Campari Group's Wild Turkey, Diageo's Bulleit, and Sazerac's Buffalo Trace.
